items.prompt: Elkanah went up yearly to worship and sacrifice to the LORD at the town marked on the map, where Eli's sons served as priests. Which town is it?
items.explanation: Elkanah went up yearly to sacrifice to the LORD of hosts in Shiloh, where Hophni and Phinehas, the sons of Eli, were priests (1 Samuel 1:3).
items.hint: The tabernacle stood here in the days of Eli, in the hill country of Ephraim.

items.prompt: David and his men went up against the Jebusites and took the stronghold of Zion, the city of David. Which marker shows Jerusalem?
items.explanation: The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, and David took the stronghold of Zion, the city of David (2 Samuel 5:6-7).
items.hint: Look in the hill country west of the northern end of the Salt Sea.

items.prompt: The Philistine champion Goliath, who challenged Israel's army, came from Gath. Which marker shows Gath?
items.explanation: Goliath, the champion of the Philistines, was 'of Gath' (1 Samuel 17:4).
items.hint: It was one of the Philistine cities, in the lowlands toward the coastal plain.

items.prompt: After Saul died in battle, the Philistines fastened his body to the wall of the city marked on the map. Which city is it?
items.explanation: The Philistines put Saul's armour in the house of Ashtaroth and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan (1 Samuel 31:10).
items.hint: This city lies where the Jezreel valley opens toward the Jordan, not far from Mount Gilboa.

items.prompt: Elisha passed through Shunem, where a great woman constrained him to eat bread. Which marker shows Shunem?
items.explanation: Elisha passed to Shunem, where a great woman constrained him to eat bread (2 Kings 4:8).
items.hint: It sits in the north, overlooking the Jezreel valley.

items.prompt: In the days of Deborah, the LORD sold Israel into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in the city marked on the map. Which city is it?
items.explanation: Jabin king of Canaan reigned in Hazor, and the captain of his host was Sisera (Judges 4:2).
items.hint: This great Canaanite city lay in upper Galilee, north of the Sea of Galilee.

items.prompt: Manoah, the father of Samson, was a man of the town marked on the map. Which town is it?
items.explanation: There was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah (Judges 13:2).
items.hint: This town of the Danites lay in the lowland hills west of Jerusalem.

items.prompt: David and his men fought the Philistines and saved the inhabitants of Keilah. Which marker shows Keilah?
items.explanation: David and his men went to Keilah, fought with the Philistines, and saved the inhabitants of Keilah (1 Samuel 23:5).
items.hint: It lay in the territory of Judah, in the lowlands northwest of Hebron.

items.prompt: While David tarried at Jerusalem, Joab and Israel's army destroyed the children of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. Which marker shows Rabbah?
items.explanation: David sent Joab and all Israel, and they destroyed the children of Ammon and besieged Rabbah, while David tarried still at Jerusalem (2 Samuel 11:1).
items.hint: The Ammonite royal city lay east of the Jordan.

items.prompt: After the ark was returned by the Philistines, men came and fetched it up to the house of Abinadab in the town marked on the map. Which town is it?
items.explanation: The men of Kirjath-jearim fetched up the ark of the LORD and brought it into the house of Abinadab (1 Samuel 7:1).
items.hint: This hill town lay a short way west of Jerusalem, on the border of Judah and Benjamin.

batch.topic: the judges, Samuel, Saul, David and Solomon, and the prophets Elijah and Elisha

items.prompt: Paul told the chief captain in Jerusalem that he was a Jew of the city marked on the map, 'a city in Cilicia.' Which city is it?
items.explanation: Paul said, 'I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city' (Acts 21:39).
items.hint: Saul is often identified by this hometown.

items.prompt: While Paul was at Troas, a vision of a man of Macedonia called him to come over and help. Which marker shows Troas?
items.explanation: Passing by Mysia, Paul's company came down to Troas, where a vision of a man of Macedonia appeared to Paul in the night (Acts 16:8-9).
items.hint: Look for a port in northwest Asia Minor facing Macedonia across the sea.

items.prompt: Hurrying toward Jerusalem, Paul stopped at the place marked on the map and sent for the elders of the church at Ephesus. Which place is it?
items.explanation: 'And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church' (Acts 20:17).
items.hint: It is a coastal city south of Ephesus.

items.prompt: Laodicea was one of the seven churches in Asia to which John was told to send what he saw. Which marker shows Laodicea?
items.explanation: John was told to send the book 'unto the seven churches which are in Asia,' ending with Laodicea (Revelation 1:11).
items.hint: The seven churches were in the province of Asia, in the west of Asia Minor.

items.prompt: Paul and Barnabas went together into the synagogue of the Jews in the city marked on the map, and a great multitude believed. Which city is it?
items.explanation: In Iconium Paul and Barnabas went into the synagogue and so spake that a great multitude of Jews and Greeks believed (Acts 14:1).
items.hint: It lies inland in south-central Asia Minor, visited before Lystra and Derbe.

items.prompt: After being stoned at Lystra, Paul departed the next day with Barnabas to Derbe and preached there. Which marker shows Derbe?
items.explanation: After Paul was stoned at Lystra, 'the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe' and preached the gospel to that city (Acts 14:19-21).
items.hint: It is in inland Asia Minor, not far from Lystra.

items.prompt: Sent forth by the Holy Ghost, Barnabas and Saul went down to Seleucia and sailed to the island marked on the map. Which island is it?
items.explanation: Being sent forth by the Holy Ghost, they 'departed unto Seleucia; and from thence they sailed to Cyprus' (Acts 13:4).
items.hint: It is the large island in the eastern corner of the Mediterranean.

items.prompt: Passing through Amphipolis and Apollonia, Paul came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews. Which marker shows Thessalonica?
items.explanation: Paul and Silas 'came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews' (Acts 17:1).
items.hint: Look in Macedonia, in northern Greece.

items.prompt: Cornelius, a centurion of the Italian band, lived in Caesarea. Which marker shows Caesarea?
items.explanation: 'There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band' (Acts 10:1).
items.hint: It is a port on the coast of the Holy Land.

items.prompt: Paul wrote to Titus that he had left him on the island marked on the map to set things in order and ordain elders in every city. Which island is it?
items.explanation: Paul told Titus, 'For this cause left I thee in Crete,' to set in order the things wanting and ordain elders (Titus 1:4-5).
items.hint: It is a long island south of the Greek mainland.

batch.topic: the journeys of Paul and his companions, the early church and the seven churches of Revelation
